To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in a prospective cohort study of 24, 323 Germans with an average follow-up of 11 year
we observed no statistically significant association between high calcium and magnesium intake and a reduced risk of cancer in a German prospective population.
dietary calcium intake is not associated with colorectal or lung cancer risk and is not associated with any site-specific or overall incidence or mortality of cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of dietary factors in the development of chronic diseases, particularly cancer.
the role of dietary factors in cancer prevention and their potential role in the development of cancer.
the association of dietary calcium and dietary magnesium intake with the risk of cancer incidence and mortality.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
dietary calcium and magnesium are not associated with cancer incidence or mortality.
dietary calcium and magnesium intakes in the range observed in the EPIC-Heidelberg cohort are not related to cancer incidence or mortality.
dietary calcium intake may not be associated with cancer risk and mortality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the intake of dietary calcium and dietary magnesium in the range observed in the German EPIC-Heidelberg cohort was not associated with cancer incidence and cancer mortality.
there is no strong evidence that a higher intake of dietary calcium or magnesium reduces cancer risk.
dietary calcium intake is associated with a lower risk of colorectal and lung cancer, while dietary magnesium intake was not significantly associated with cancer incidence or mortality.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the intake of calcium from food sources is not associated with cancer risk.
there was no association with dietary calcium and magnesium and the risk of developing cancer.
there is no evidence that calcium and magnesium are protective against cancer.
